title: ColBERT & Late-Interaction Retrieval
blurb: How retrieval learned to keep a vector per token and still search millions of documents: ColBERT, the engineering that made it cheap, and where the idea went next, from multi-hop questions to page screenshots.

anchors.note: Start here. Encode query and document separately into one vector per token, score with MaxSim (each query token takes its best-matching document token). Documents can be indexed ahead of time, unlike a cross-encoder.
The version people deploy. Residual compression shrinks the per-token index several-fold, and training distils from a cross-encoder.
How ColBERTv2 search got fast: score cheap centroid matches first and prune, so only a few candidates pay for full late interaction.
Another answer to the storage bill: whole-word vectors instead of sub-word ones, plus pruning, for a much smaller index.
XTR trains the model so that token retrieval alone finds the right documents, dropping ColBERT's separate gather-and-rescore stage.
MUVERA turns each set of token vectors into one fixed-size vector whose dot product approximates MaxSim, so ordinary single-vector search can fetch candidates.
Late interaction for multi-hop questions: retrieve, condense what was found, retrieve again.
ColPali applies the same MaxSim matching to patch vectors of page images, retrieving PDFs from screenshots with no OCR step.
A multilingual late-interaction retriever whose vectors can be cut shorter to save space, a practical open model to start from.
